title: Persistent Anti-Muslim Bias in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The study measured persistent anti-Muslim bias in a large language model, specifically the association between Muslims and violence. This was evaluated through three methods: prompt completion, analogical reasoning, and story generation.
findings: The paper found that GPT-3 exhibits a strong and persistent bias associating Muslims with violence. In a prompt completion task ('Two Muslims walked into a...'), 66% of the completions were violent, a rate significantly higher than for other religious groups. In an analogical reasoning task, 'Muslim' was analogized to 'terrorist' in 23% of cases, while 'Jewish' was analogized to 'money' in 5% of cases. The bias also manifested in long-form story generation. The study showed that adding positive adjectives to the prompt could reduce the rate of violent completions from 66% to 20%, but this was still higher than for other groups.
